2	
3	Prelude's home page (`/`), today `server/views/_home.eta`: an "Open a project"
4	form and a list of recent projects (name and path only). This design turns it
5	into a dashboard across the person's projects: "what needs me, and where was I?"
6	
7	Pages: `/` (Home), `/loading` (Home before its regions load; the design's way
8	to show it, not a URL the app needs), `/open` (the modal). States: typical,
9	first run (no projects), all caught up, long names.
10	
11	## Decisions
12	
13	- **Across projects** (the person's decision, 2026-10-16). Each project's own
14	  page keeps its full "In progress"; home gathers the parts that need action.
15	- **Needs you includes finished turns and questions** (the person, 2026-10-16),
16	  beside "ready to build", "build stopped" and "pull request open". Each row
17	  links to where it's answered; a pull request opens on the Git server.
18	  What's running right now stays in the bar, not repeated here.
19	- **Projects as a grid of cards** (a handful, the person said): each with its
20	  in-progress designs as links, how many things are waiting on you, and a line
21	  of facts (designs, stack, last change).
22	- **Regions load separately, with skeletons** (the person asked for loading
23	  states). The page arrives with the recent list (cheap); Needs you
24	  (`/home/needs-you`) and the projects' contents (`/home/projects`) each load

5	- **R-8hc.** A turn that ended with an error leaves Needs you once the person has opened its session, or after a week if they never do; a turn that finished well isn't listed.
6	- **R-w2k.** A pull request isn't in Needs you: its project's In progress says it's open until it's merged.

11	- **R-p6r.** While the home page is open, what needs the person and what's in each project refresh on their own as soon as something changes in Prelude, and every five minutes for changes made elsewhere (not while the window is hidden).
12	- **R-h9b.** A recent project whose folder has gone stays listed, saying so, until the person removes it; removing it leaves the disk alone.
13	  *shown-on: /*
14	- **R-z3g.** The bar shows how many things are waiting on the person across all their projects, and leads home; it shows nothing when none are.
15	- **R-d0y.** If Prelude can't read part of the home page, that part says so and offers to try again, and the rest of the page still works.

The fix belongs in the app's code, not in this design. The design's projects list doesn't need any changes; the app is passing the wrong folders into it.

**Cause:** Prelude keeps one folder per design branch under `~/.prelude/worktrees/…`. A branch folder lands in the recent list if it's ever opened as a plain folder, as older builds did. Nothing removes branch folders when the projects list is read (`app.folders.recent()`, used at `server/home.js:292`). That's why you see `prelude-landing-page` next to `Prelude`, and other branch folders marked "gone" once their branches were merged.

**What I changed:**
- **`RULES.md`:** added R-c7w (*proposed*), shown on `/`: "Only projects are listed: the folders Prelude makes to work on a design's branch never appear as projects of their own, even one opened directly, and their work shows in their project's card instead."
- **`NOTES.md`:** recorded the cause and the fix: leave branch folders out of the recent list and delete their old entries.

The build will make the rule true. If you want it fixed sooner than the next build of Home, it could also go in as a fix in the project.
